title: Acute appendicitis: from blocked lumen to the right decision
summary: Work out why appendicitis hurts where it does, read the signs, choose the right test for each patient and decide who needs the knife, antibiotics or a drain.
closing: You can now follow the appendix from blocked lumen to operating table: the right sign, the right scan and the right plan for each patient.

objectives.text: Name acute appendicitis as the commonest abdominal surgical emergency, including in pregnancy
Choose the usual obstructing cause for a child versus an adult
Order the events from luminal obstruction to pain shifting to the right iliac fossa, and say why the end artery matters
Pick the true order of symptoms (pain, then vomiting, then fever) and spot a story that does not fit
Tell psoas, obturator and Rovsing signs apart and tie each to the appendix position it suggests
Use the Alvarado score: which items score 2, and what the cut-offs mean
Choose the first imaging test for an adult, a child and a pregnant woman
Pick the step that comes before imaging or surgery in a woman, and the look-alike diagnoses for RIF pain by group
Choose between appendicectomy and antibiotics-first for a given patient
Choose the management of an appendicular mass versus an abscess, and when interval surgery applies
Separate complications of the disease from complications of appendicectomy, and name the nerve at risk with a gridiron incision
Name the commonest appendix tumour and the size rule the PYQ key uses

traps.trap: Psoas and obturator manoeuvres are swapped
Each sign is tied to the wrong appendix position
Rovsing's sign is reversed
Pain pathway and causal chain are reversed (RIF first then umbilical; ischaemia before obstruction)
Symptom order reversed (vomiting before pain)
Alvarado weighting and cut-offs are misremembered (migration or rebound scored 2; score read as diagnostic)
A negative ultrasound excludes appendicitis in an adult
CT is used as the first test in children and pregnant women
MRI is chosen as the first-line test in pregnancy
The old PYQ key (ultrasound as investigation of choice in general) is applied to adults
Pregnancy test is skipped before imaging or surgery in a woman of reproductive age
A different condition is picked as the most common abdominal surgical emergency
RIF pain always means appendicitis
Obstruction cause is age-blind (faecolith in the child, lymphoid hyperplasia in the adult)
Disease complications are merged with complications of appendicectomy
Nerve injured by a gridiron incision is named wrongly
Appendicectomy is the only treatment for appendicitis
Antibiotics-first is offered to a patient with an appendicolith or complicated disease
Interval appendicectomy at 6-8 weeks is applied routinely after an appendicular mass
Immediate surgery for an appendicular mass or open drainage for an abscess

segments.title: Most common, and why it blocks
segments.goal: Learner commits on the commonest surgical emergency and the age-linked cause of obstruction before any teaching.

prefer.reason: Playbook: retrieval-gate hooks that let the learner fail a real stem first have won.

segments.title: From blocked lumen to shifting pain
segments.goal: Learner predicts and orders the chain obstruction, pressure, ischaemia, then visceral-to-somatic pain, and the symptom sequence.

segments.title: Reading the right iliac fossa
segments.goal: Learner links signs to manoeuvres and to appendix position, applies Alvarado, and meets the first look-alike.

prefer.reason: Psoas, obturator and Rovsing are one look-alike set; side-by-side contrast fits the E1 repair.

segments.title: Which test, for whom
segments.goal: Learner picks the first test by patient group and keeps the pregnancy test and the PYQ-versus-current ultrasound and CT point straight.

prefer.reason: Playbook: faded worked example with a skip lane wins investigation segments.

segments.title: Operate, wait, or drain
segments.goal: Learner chooses treatment for uncomplicated disease, antibiotics-first candidates, mass and abscess, and meets post-operative complications.

prefer.reason: Planted-error management plans map directly onto TR22, TR24 and TR25, after a correct worked case.

segments.title: Exam traps and unaided check
segments.goal: Cold, hint-free mixed probes re-test every backbone trap in a new form and close with the tumour key.
